verdict.rationale: Nitrokey's own docs list "SSH Keys" under its FIDO2 features, and the product page advertises SSH login using certificates. The OpenPGP card docs add on-device key generation and touch confirmation on the Nitrokey 3, and PIV is a documented feature. The evidence is mostly section headings, though, and none of it explicitly ties the touch requirement to SSH authentication. missing for 10: detailed sk-ssh/ed25519-sk setup documentation, explicit statement that SSH auth requires touch for FIDO2 and PIV keys, documented PIV-based SSH workflow, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, my SSH keys can be hardware-backed on the device — via FIDO2 sk-ssh keys, PIV, or OpenPGP — so server access requires a physical touch

citations.quote: Login to computers and network services (e.g. SSH) using certificates.
